subject: Deployment mode clarification — latency & throughput for QuikCart
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: alex.chen@quikcart.com, sofia.ramos@quikcart.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode clarification — latency & throughput for QuikCart

Alex / Sofia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we’re aligned on the decision factors and next steps. I’ve pulled the notes into bullets to make the tradeoffs explicit for your infra and product teams.

Summary of constraints you shared:
- P95 inference latency target: 120ms (user-facing quick search flows)
- Average sequence length: ~60 tokens for queries, 200 tokens for long-form assistants (less frequent)
- Steady-state QPS: ~200 requests/sec, but you mentioned burst windows up to ~800 QPS for marketing events (3–5 min peaks)
- Concurrency: peaks can hit ~1,500 concurrent sessions across devices during campaigns
- Data residency: US-only; no on-prem requirement for initial pilot
- Security posture: SOC2 required; custom question set coming from procurement

Initial recommendation (based on performance and economics):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the conservative recommendation to meet sustained 200 QPS + P95 120ms reliably while enabling predictable tail-latency behavior during bursts.
- Hosted API could be feasible if we combine: aggressive batching config, prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and our burst autoscaling policy with dedicated warm pools. This is lower friction but carries variability during extreme peaks unless we provision burst capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is not necessary for pilot but remains an option for later compliance/air-gap requirements.

Concrete next steps we propose:
1) You share 24–48 hours of representative payloads (attachments: quikcart_sample_payloads.json) so we can run a focused benchmark with your sequence distribution.
2) We’ll run a 3-day benchmark (Redwood benchmark template attached) and return measured P50/P95/P99 latencies and cost projection for Hosted vs Dedicated.
3) Marissa to sync on pricing trigger for Dedicated (monthly commit & burst allowance).
4) Karthik and I to run a short PoC (2–3 weeks) if benchmarks look good.
5) Procurement: please send SOC2 questionnaire; we’ve attached our certificate.

I’ll schedule the benchmark kickoff once we have the sample payloads and confirmation that we should include the marketing-burst profile in the run. If you’d like, we can also include a quick run of our prefix-caching config to show how much Hosted can buy you on unit cost for the long-tail requests.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: quikcart_sample_payloads.json, redwood_benchmark_template.xlsx, soc2_certificate.pdf

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@quikcart.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: sofia.ramos@quikcart.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode clarification — latency & throughput for QuikCart

Lauren — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few points from our side:
- The 800 QPS bursts are accurate and usually last 3–7 minutes; they are quite spiky and driven by ad pushes.
- We care most about P95 for product search (target 120ms), P99 can be higher for async recommendations.
- We’ll share payloads later today (privacy-filtered) and include a short description of which traffic profiles map to search vs recommendations.

Two asks: can your benchmark run include a simulated upstream cache-miss scenario? Also, curious on the expected lead time for switching from Hosted to Dedicated if we start on Hosted and decide to move.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Engineering, QuikCart
alex.chen@quikcart.com

Lauren / Karthik — quick internal: I agree Dedicated is the safer path if they expect sustained 200 QPS and those 800 QPS bursts. A couple of operational notes to include in the benchmark:
- Run a mixed-load profile: 70% short queries (<=64 tokens) at high QPS + 30% long assistants to capture KV cache efficacy.
- Include a cold-start run (no KV caching) and a warm-run (with prefix caching) so we can show gating impact on P95.
- For Hosted cost model, include our burst-rate tier pricing and a hypothetical warm-pool reserve that limits tail latency deviation during 3–7 min spikes.

I’ll draft the pricing trigger language for Dedicated (scale bands, burst allowance, SLA targets) after we get benchmark numbers.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Deployment mode clarification — latency & throughput for QuikCart

Alex / Sofia — quick follow-up with answers and final asks before we kick off the benchmark.

Answers to Alex’s asks:
- Yes, we will include an explicit cache-miss scenario in the benchmark (cold-run) and the warm-run to show delta with prefix/KV caching.
- Switching lead time: if you start on Hosted and want to move to Dedicated, typical timeline is 3–6 weeks for Dedicated provisioning and warm-up (depending on commitment and region). We’ll include a migration playbook in the PoC.

Final items we need from QuikCart to start (please upload to the Drive link or reply here):
1) Representative payloads (privacy-filtered) — includes examples for search and recommendation paths.
2) Burst schedule or calendar events when you expect marketing pushes in the next 30 days (so we can align runs).
3) SOC2 questionnaire (if procurement wants to run in parallel).

Marissa: can you own the benchmark config and include cost modeling slides? Karthik: please plan to join the kickoff call and own the migration playbook review. Mina: I’ve cc’d you to loop Customer Success in early.

Next meeting: I’ll propose two 30-minute windows tomorrow morning to review the run plan before we start.

Thanks — Lauren
